description: Michigan-only rules checked against the Michigan Vehicle Code through Public Act 103 of 2026. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Michigan's statutory speed on a highway segment within the boundaries of a mobile home park is
questions.explanation: MCL 257.627(2)(a) sets 15 mph on a highway segment within the boundaries of a mobile home park. The section does not use that number as a statewide school-zone speed.

questions.q: The speed Michigan sets on a highway segment within a business district is
questions.explanation: MCL 257.627(2)(b) sets 25 mph within a business district. A public park is also 25 under (2)(c), and a local authority may decrease a park limit to not less than 15.

questions.q: The limited-access freeway general speed limit is 70 mph. That limit is not valid unless
options: The freeway is rural, even with no sign
questions.explanation: MCL 257.627(8) names 70 mph as the limited-access freeway general speed limit where a speed is not otherwise fixed. Subsection (12) says speed limits other than those in subsections (1), (2)(d), (2)(e), and (9) are not valid unless properly posted. The 70 mph freeway limit is not in that exception. Without a proper sign the basic speed law applies.

questions.q: On trunk line highways and county highways where a speed limit is not otherwise fixed, Michigan's general speed limit is
options: 65 mph and it must be posted before it applies
55 mph, valid even without a posted sign
questions.explanation: MCL 257.627(9) sets 55 mph as the general speed limit on those highways. Subsection (12) excepts subsection (9) from the rule that a speed limit is invalid until posted.

questions.q: Michigan defines operating while intoxicated to include an alcohol content of 0.08 grams or more per
options: 100 ml blood, 210 liters breath, or 67 ml urine
210 liters of breath only, with no blood measure
questions.explanation: MCL 257.625(1)(b) uses those three measures. A 0.10 figure replaces 0.08 only beginning five years after the state treasurer publishes the certification described in subsection (28). 100 milliliters of blood, 210 liters of breath, or 67 milliliters of urine.

questions.q: A person under 21 may not operate a vehicle with any bodily alcohol content. That phrase includes
options: Only a result of 0.08 or more
0.02 up to under 0.08 grams, or any alcohol except from a religious service
Any presence of alcohol, including alcohol consumed as part of a religious service
questions.explanation: MCL 257.625(6) defines any bodily alcohol content in those two ways. The 0.02-to-under-0.08 branch also changes to under 0.10 only after the subsection (28) certification period. An alcohol content of 0.02 grams or more but less than 0.08 grams per 100 milliliters of blood, 210 liters of breath, or 67 milliliters of urine, or any presence of alcohol from consumption other than as part of a generally recognized religious service or ceremony.

questions.q: The secretary of state may investigate a driver, and may then restrict, suspend, or revoke the license, when the driver has
options: 12 or more points within two years
3 moving violations of any point value
questions.explanation: MCL 257.320(1)(d) includes a total of 12 or more points as provided in section 320a within two years. Subsection (2) allows restriction, suspension, revocation, or other conditions. Subsection (4) says a license shall not be suspended under this section for more than one year.

questions.q: A level 1 driver may operate only when accompanied by a licensed parent or legal guardian or, with that person's permission, a licensed driver 21 or older, and must remain at level 1 for at least
questions.explanation: MCL 257.310e(4) states the accompanier rule and the minimum of six months at level 1, except as otherwise provided in the section.

questions.q: A level 2 license requires a parent or guardian certification of at least
questions.explanation: MCL 257.310e(5)(d) requires not less than 50 hours, including not less than 10 nighttime hours, with a licensed parent or guardian or, with permission, any licensed driver 21 or older. The nighttime-hour requirement does not apply to a daylight-only graduated license under R 257.3. 50 hours of behind-the-wheel experience, including at least 10 nighttime hours.

questions.q: In Michigan, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Michigan issues a learner's permit for a car at 14 years and 9 months at the earliest.

questions.q: In Michigan, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Michigan requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Michigan complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Michigan requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Michigan teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Michigan requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

questions.q: In Michigan, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Michigan, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Michigan not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Michigan restricts provisional drivers from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

questions.q: In Michigan, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Michigan drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Michigan car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Michigan car knowledge test has 50 questions.

provenance.manual: DES - 201 Driver Education Curriculum Guide - State of Michigan

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Michigan car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 70% to pass the Michigan car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Michigan, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Michigan, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

provenance.manual: MCL 257.625 Operating motor vehicle while intoxicated

questions.q: In Michigan, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Michigan sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

provenance.manual: MCL 257.625 Operating motor vehicle while intoxicated

questions.q: In Michigan, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Michigan brings a suspension of 1 year.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Michigan residential district?
questions.explanation: Michigan sets 25 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Michigan?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Michigan can be posted up to 75 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes Michigan's law on drivers using a phone?
options: No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
questions.explanation: Michigan: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: Distracted Driving Awareness Month will focus on enforcing Hands

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Michigan?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Michigan, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: from a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street.

provenance.manual: What Every Driver Must Know - State of Michigan

questions.q: How is Michigan's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: Michigan seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: Office of Highway Safety Planning - State of Michigan

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Michigan?
questions.explanation: Michigan requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

questions.q: What is Michigan's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Michigan requires at least $50,000 / $100,000 / $10,000.

provenance.manual: What Every Driver Must Know - State of Michigan

questions.q: Under Michigan's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Michigan can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 24 months.
